notes: oracle tiers (item fathomcue, calibration/oracles/fathom-cue): sym_* (L1) and ref_* (L2) are tier A. The oracle is the cue binary v0.16.1 as separate processes, never fathom's loader: `cue export --out json` names what exists (including what a comprehension generates, which only evaluation names), `cue lsp` documentSymbol gives each range and textDocument/definition each reference (calibration/oracles/cue). A written entity's range is the language server's field; a generated one's is the dynamic field it lists. Structure is graded beside the metrics, tier A and not one of them: cue vet -d against schema/project, schema/semantic and schema/rules/archconformance passes on all fixtures. The repository's own files are one layer.cue (ui-appkit) and one rule pack (archconformance) and have no reference a language server resolves (the rule pack's list is a let, which is no entity), so all 5 references (L2) are on the in-repo fixture calibration/oracles/fathom-cue/fixtures/layer-packs (budgets naming a hidden table; a rule pack comprehension over one), whose subject sha is the fathom commit measured at: L2 rests on it. The repository subject alone reads L1 excellent and no L2 evidence. The subjects are tiny (4 entities): the throughput gate reads a first-run value under 1 MB/s on the repository subject alone, and the committed reading is the merged run that met it

scope: one entity per layer.cue (named by its `name`) and per rule file (named by its stem, spanning `rules:`). Not read: the individual rules of a pack (list elements have no symbol in the language server, so no tier A range), the corpus and prompt_file paths (cross-file, L3)
per-file times exclude the one-time grammar compile (an untimed warm-up extraction precedes timing)
